//: Type checking for a plain-JavaScript project.
Handrail has no TypeScript and is not gaining any. What this buys instead is
the half of a type checker that works without annotations: calls to functions
that do not exist, properties read off the wrong shape, arity mistakes, and
typos in an Electron API name. `strict` is off deliberately — turning it on
an unannotated codebase produces thousands of implicit-any complaints that
say nothing about correctness and would guarantee nobody ever runs this.
Renderer files are excluded: they run in a DOM context against a preload
bridge injected at runtime, so the checker cannot see `window.handrail` and
reports every use of it as an error.
